title: Rhaita
summary: The rhaita is a double-reed oboe of the Maghreb. A slim dark body carries a small brass-coloured disc at the lips and opens into a short flaring bell. Its sound is piercing and nasal, made to carry over drums at weddings and festivals.
howToPlay: A covered hole glows; an open hole shows its dark bore. Seven notes of the mode are lit down the tube.
Each strike shows the fingering of that note and the bell opens as it sounds.
Keep the phrases lively and the long notes steady.
rules: A phrase is a line of notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It leads the processions and dance bands of Morocco and its neighbours, where it plays above the drums.
